name: Dextrose in lactated Ringer’s solution

sources.citation: Baxter. Lactated Ringer’s and Dextrose (5%) Injection. FDA labeling revised October 2025; Reference ID5690093. Standard D5LR portion of combined label, not the potassium-chloride-added products. US reference formulation.

FDA Philippines. Product registration fields retained in the website dataset; exact formulations and current status require verification against the approved product insert. Reviewed 25 November 2026.

draft_notes: Product-specific Philippine instructions remain to be verified. No unverified composition, preservative assumption or renal replacement regimen is assigned.

revision_log.change: Faithfully attributed regulatory safety summary or descriptive guideline/registry findings; no unsupported dose or personal physician review claimed.
revision_log.approved_by: Codex source verification under existing delegated workflow.

overview.mechanism: The cited US D5LR supplies water, dextrose, sodium, potassium, calcium and lactate [[D5LRUS]].
uses: US reference: water, electrolyte and calorie supply or alkalinization; verify the exact Philippine composition [[D5LRUS,PHREG]].

usual_adult_dose.dose: Volume and duration depend on age, weight, clinical state and other therapy; no fixed rate is assigned across these registry products [[D5LRUS]].

contraindications: US reference: ceftriaxone treatment in neonates aged 28 days or younger; component hypersensitivity; clinically significant hyperglycemia [[D5LRUS]].

serious: Fluid overload, hyperkalemia, hyponatremia, hyperglycemia and acid–base disturbances [[D5LRUS]].

monitoring: Fluid balance, electrolytes, glucose and acid–base status; neonatal glucose requires close monitoring [[D5LRUS]].

key_interactions.action: Contraindicated with ceftriaxone in neonates ≤28 days; in older patients, sequential use requires thorough line flushing [[D5LRUS]].

renal: The cited US D5LR label advises avoiding use in severe renal impairment because of overload/solute risks. If unavoidable, closely monitor fluid balance, electrolytes and acid–base status [[D5LRUS]].
hepatic: US reference: avoid severe hepatic impairment; if unavoidable, monitor bicarbonate because lactate metabolism may be impaired [[D5LRUS]].

rows.findings: Do not administer simultaneously with citrate-anticoagulated/preserved blood through the same administration set; calcium/ceftriaxone and glucose-related risks require attention.
rows.limitations: Not the potassium-chloride-added products in the same combined FDA PDF; not a blanket Philippine-product dose.

rows.design: 12 direct records plus four related spelling-variant records.
rows.intervention: Products with differing or incompletely stated quantities.
rows.findings: Some recorded concentrations/units are inconsistent; the page preserves them and flags verification.
rows.limitations: No guessed correction or assumption that all brands have the US composition.
